Review completed with 2 findings across 2 agents (2 critical).

⚠️ 2 critical/high severity issues require immediate attention:
  - [CRITICAL] Removal of Template Injection Validation (LogicAgent)
  - [CRITICAL] Reintroduction of Command Injection via _.template variable option (SecurityAgent)

findings.title: Removal of Template Injection Validation
findings.description: The diff removes the `INVALID_TEMPL_VAR_ERROR_TEXT` constant and the corresponding validation logic that prevented code injection through the `variable` option in `_.template`. This change introduces a critical security vulnerability (Server-Side Template Injection / Arbitrary Code Execution) in the lodash library. While this falls under security, it also represents a regression in error handling and input validation logic that was specifically designed to mitigate a class of bugs/exploits.
findings.suggestion: Revert the changes that remove the `reForbiddenIdentifierChars` regex and the validation check in `_.template`. The security patch must be restored. If the intent was to remove this feature, it should not be merged into a main branch of a public library without a security review.

findings.title: Reintroduction of Command Injection via _.template variable option
findings.description: The removal of the `reForbiddenIdentifierChars` validation check in `lodash.js` allows user-controlled input passed to the `variable` option of `_.template` to contain special characters. This re-introduces a command injection vulnerability in the generated template code. An attacker can supply a `variable` string containing characters like `(){}`, `=`, `,`, `/`, or whitespace to manipulate the generated `with (variable) { ... }` block, potentially executing arbitrary JavaScript code in the context of the application.
findings.suggestion: Re-introduce the validation check that forbids the use of special characters in the `variable` option. You must ensure that the `reForbiddenIdentifierChars` regex and the corresponding `throw new Error(INVALID_TEMPL_VAR_ERROR_TEXT)` block are restored to prevent code injection.
